title: Surge-induced TTFT regression: mixed-model routing + prefetch throttle hotfix
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
During a sustained customer traffic surge on 2026-03-09 we observed a cross-environment TTFT regression impacting Hosted and Dedicated customers. The regression manifested as elevated first-token time (median increased ~3.7x) and a ~25% drop in tokens/sec for mixed-model routes that route between rw-13b-v2 and quantized rw-7b variants. Private deployments with strict prewarming also saw tail latency increases when requests hit recently scaled instances.

Observed symptoms and telemetry:
- Median TTFT for affected routes rose from ~85ms to ~320ms within a 30-minute window at 09:42 UTC.
- Aggregate tokens/sec for the pool fell ~25% during surge.
- Per-instance kernel warm ratio (estimated from KV cache hits + per-process kernel load time) dropped significantly; CPU/GPU utilization stayed high.
- Errors were not increased, but queuing latency and head-of-line blocking were evident in request traces.

Root cause hypothesis (triage findings):
- A routing optimization deployed in runtime-1.22 changed the route-affinity key to include a non-stable field (session_hint) to improve locality for LLM-chat use cases. Under bursty traffic this resulted in high cardinality affinity keys causing frequent cold starts for kernels and KV caches for certain tenants.
- The kernel scheduler's heuristic to prefer freshly compiled kernels over warmed-but-older kernels caused additional context-switching on GPUs under mixed workloads; combined with the higher cold-start rate this amplified TTFT and reduced sustained tokens/sec.
- Prefetch throttling we added for aggressive memory-constrained tenants interacted poorly: it deferred KV prefetch during spikes, increasing initial decode work.

Immediate mitigations applied (hotfix path):
1) Rollback partial routing-affinity change for Hosted/Dedicated traffic while preserving improved locality via a safer stable-key path. (PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/4521)
2) Patch kernel scheduler fallback to prefer warmed kernel instances when warm_ratio > 0.3; new heuristic reduces kernel churn during surges. (PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/4523)
3) Disable the aggressive prefetch throttle for A/B cohorts and enable conservative prewarming for high-burst tenants (feature flag: prefetch.throttle.conservative=true).
4) Apply per-tenant burst shaping on the edge to smooth requests for 24 hours for the top 10 impacted customers.

Results from hotfix (canary -> production):
- Canary (10% traffic) showed median TTFT drop from 320ms -> 90ms and tokens/sec recovery +28% within 5 minutes of hotfix rollout.
- Full rollout (after 30m observation window) returned metrics close to baseline across Hosted and Dedicated pools.

Next steps and follow-ups (backlog items):
- ENG follow-up: Add deterministic unit and e2e tests for route-affinity key behavior (ENG-30111).
- Runtime improvements: Expose kernel warm_ratio and kernel_fallback_decision as stable metrics and add alerting thresholds.
- Console/Observability: Dashboard tile for instance_warm_ratio and per-tenant surge alerts; add correlation chart between affinity-cardinality and TTFT.
- Docs: Update runbook (runbooks/latency-regression.md) with the new rollback/playbook steps and add KB entry for customers describing temporary burst shaping.
- Long-term: Replace the ad-hoc scheduler heuristic with a latency-aware scheduler evaluated under mixed-model workloads (spike + multi-tenant) in perf lab.

Customer communications:
- Notified top 8 impacted customers via CSMs with summary and ETA for permanent mitigations.
- Status page postmortem draft is under review in Confluence.

Questions/risks:
- Private/on-prem deployments: some customers may not accept automatic rollback. For those we published a hotfix package and guided upgrades (ENG-30112).
- Edge burst-shaping may delay some low-priority requests; ensure SLAs for P0 customers remain honored.
